thread:
kai: rolled the new batching heuristic (token_budget target changed from 0.7 -> 0.45) to canary tonight at 02:30 UTC. seeing p95 generation latency up ~35-50ms and overall throughput down ~10% on the canary pool. anyone else seeing this?
marta: yup I flipped on observability dashboards — latency jump correlates with an uptick in tiny-batch count. looks like more 1-3 token microbatches.
ravi: adding context: kernel selection traces show a higher fraction of requests hitting the slow 'large-kernel' path even for short sequences. might be batch shape churn causing kernel rebinds.
anya: hm that sounds like batch formation churn. the heuristic now aggressively flushes when token_budget remaining < 0.45, so it terminates batches sooner -> more uneven shapes. can you paste the batching histogram?
kai: here (snippet from the dashboard):
```
batch_size_hist: {1: 24%, 2-4: 46%, 5-8: 20%, 9+: 10%}
prev_baseline: {1: 8%, 2-4: 30%, 5-8: 35%, 9+: 27%}
```
marta: wow 1-token batches triple. also KV-cache hit rate dropped ~6% on the canary. likely because many requests don't get aggregated enough to reuse KV across cache windows.
ravi: can confirm from profiler: increased kernel selection metadata churn. the runtime's kernel affinity table is flipping on a per-batch basis, causing additional kernel preloads (~8-12ms per flip).
anya: TLDR: heuristic flush threshold reduced the tail of token budgets, creating many tiny batches -> kernel thrash + worse KV reuse -> latency + throughput regression.
kai: infra-bot reports a small rise in context-switch counts on the worker processes around deployment time. might be related to more frequent batch completions triggering scheduling overhead.

marta: quick mitigation options: 1) revert to previous token_budget 0.7; 2) change queue_policy to prefer joining when same model+context_size present for X ms; 3) add short coalescing delay for workers with <3 tokens in batch.
ravi: we should also consider kernel stabilization: if batch shape changes rapidly within 50ms window, keep using previous kernel for an extra step to avoid reloads. cheap guard.
anya: agree. reversing the token_budget seems the fastest rollback. I'm going to patch canary config to 0.65 and monitor.
kai: please also enable detailed per-worker KV hit tracing for next 10m so we can quantify reuse delta.
anya: done. toggled to 0.65 at 02:47 UTC. canary metrics starting to move back toward baseline.
marta: KV hit rate recovered to +4% from the trough in ~3 min. p95 latency back down ~20ms of the spike. throughput recovering.
ravi: past profiler run (during spike) attached below:
```
# top stack samples
45% runtime::dispatch -> kernel_selector::choose -> kernel_loader::load_if_mismatch
18% runtime::batcher -> batcher::flush_if_budget_under
12% runtime::kvcache -> kv::lookup_miss_handling
8% runtime::scheduler -> schedule_wakeup
```
kai: that stack matches the hypothesis. two actions: rollback token_budget tweak for broader rollout, and implement kernel-stability guard in next patch.
anya: filing follow-up PR to add a short kernel-holdback (50ms) and an opt-in coalesce_delay config per pool. will add unit and integration tests.
marta: i'll draft an incident note for the retro: include what changed, the observable impact, and the safe rollout checklist so future heuristic changes have a canary ramp + perf-stress test.
infra-bot: canary-config-change recorded: user=anya, field=token_budget, from=0.45, to=0.65, at=1938765467
kai: thanks. if we see any remaining ripple in the next 30m, we'll open an SRE page and escalate. for now marking this thread resolved unless new data emerges. :thumbsup:
